mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.10 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the housing market (HOUST) indicates a demand shock where consumer weakness is offset by housing strength, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as sector rotation boosts industrials and materials.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market that pressures firms to raise wages and prices, eventually leading to higher interest rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative correlation between UNRATE and returns breaks down in a rolling 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% MoM, accompanied by a concurrent rise in the S&P 500, suggests a supply-side expansion that boosts earnings expectations and drives further equity gains over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months, or the correlation between INDPRO acceleration and short-term returns turns negative for a full calendar year.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which historically has been associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to compressed real yields and earnings pressure.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the joint coefficient is not significant at p < 0.10 in a rolling regression.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals a significant labor market weakening, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as recession risk rises and corporate guidance turns cautious.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the negative correlation between PAYEMS drops and returns inverts for three consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% combined with a flat or declining GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a savings-driven demand shortfall, which tends to depress consumer spending and drag on corporate earnings, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the interaction term's t-statistic is below 1.65 in a rolling estimation window.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 returns holds when the economy is in an expansionary regime (UNRATE > 4%), implying that rising supply activity signals improving corporate fundamentals and higher equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO growth and S&P 500 20-day returns turns negative and remains below zero for a full calendar year within an expansionary regime.
